description: Deterministic linter for implementation plans and specs: validates OpenSpec and SpecKit change packages against a repository's real Makefile targets, coverage floor, waivers and witnesses.
rules: planlint is a linter and a gate, not an authoring tool. It never writes spec prose.
Read-only verbs: detect, validate, graph, rules, waivers. These never modify the target repository.
Verbs that write files: init (two files), new (three files), witness (one record under the target's hidden witness store). Both init and new accept --dry-run.

Exit codes are three-way: 0 means no findings at or above the threshold, 1 means findings were reported, 2 means a precondition or usage error such as a missing spec tree or a target path that is not a directory. Exit 2 is not a spec failure.
A nonzero exit is authoritative. Never report a pass that the tool did not report.

Waivers are inline HTML comments using the specgraph:allow prefix, which is retained as a stable identifier after the CLI was renamed to planlint. Every waiver must state a reason; a reason-less waiver is itself an error (G007).
planlint never runs make and never evaluates the target repository's file contents as code. It makes exactly one subprocess call, a read-only git rev-parse HEAD, used only for witness freshness.
Three dialects exist: harness, upstream, and speckit. The new verb scaffolds only harness and upstream packages.
Witness rules (the W family) are evaluated only when validate is passed --require-witness. A plain validate run does not check them.
